```text
Upgrade the Sehat Sahulat UI into a premium, polished healthcare SaaS product while preserving all existing functionality, routes, API behavior, and content.

- Premium, calm, trustworthy healthcare aesthetic.

- Keep the interface accessible, readable, and reassuring.
- Use generous spacing, clean typography, soft shadows, subtle borders, rounded 16–24px cards, and high-quality responsive layouts.
- Avoid anything that looks generic, overly colorful, childish, or like a basic dashboard.

- Use Sora or a similar modern display font for headings.
- Use Manrope or a similar highly readable font for body text.
- Create a clear type scale with strong hierarchy.
- Improve line-height, letter spacing, heading weights, and mobile readability.

Homepage:
- Redesign the hero into a premium split layout with:
  - Strong headline: “Your health. Clearly explained.”
  - Short supporting copy.
  - Primary CTA: “Analyze my report”.
  - Secondary CTA: “See how it works”.
  - Trust indicators such as “Private by design”, “English + Urdu”, and “Doctor-friendly guidance”.
- Improve the hero image treatment with a refined overlay, soft gradient, subtle decorative shapes, and a polished medical-report visual.
- Add a floating upload/analyze card that visually anchors the main action.
- Add a small social-proof or trust section below the hero.
- Improve the “How it works” section with premium numbered cards, icons, hover states, and a visual connecting line.
- Add a clear “Why people use Sehat Sahulat” section with three or four benefits.
- Improve the upload area with:
  - Drag-and-drop interaction.
  - Upload icon and visual feedback.
  - File type and size guidance.
  - Preview state.
  - Loading progress state.
  - Clear validation and error messages.
- Make the analysis results section feel like a premium medical report:
  - Strong summary header.
  - Urgency badge with clear color meaning.
  - Clean result table.
  - Better bilingual English/Urdu toggle.
  - Highlight abnormal values without creating panic.
  - Add an obvious medical disclaimer.
  - Make the appointment recommendation card visually prominent.
- Add a premium footer with navigation, privacy messaging, disclaimer, and contact/help links.

Navigation:
- Improve the header with a clean logo lockup, active route states, responsive mobile menu, and a prominent “Analyze report” CTA.
- Add subtle sticky-header behavior on scroll.
- Ensure navigation remains accessible with keyboard focus states.

How It Works page:
- Redesign it as a visual step-by-step journey.
- Use a timeline or connected process layout for the four AI agents.
- Add elegant icon cards, step numbers, explanatory copy, and a final CTA.
- Add a polished FAQ accordion with smooth open/close behavior.

AI Mentor page:
- Make it feel like a premium conversational health assistant.
- Add a refined chat header with status indicator.
- Improve empty state with suggested questions.
- Style user and assistant messages clearly.
- Add loading animation, error state, retry action, and bilingual support.
- Keep the interface calm and professional, not like a social chat app.
- Add a visible “Educational guidance only — not a diagnosis” notice.

Interaction and motion:
- Add subtle fade-up and slide-in animations.
- Use smooth hover transitions and button feedback.
- Add skeleton loaders where appropriate.
- Avoid excessive animation or anything distracting.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

Responsive behavior:
- Optimize carefully for mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- Ensure all cards, forms, tables, buttons, and navigation work well on small screens.
- Never allow horizontal overflow.
- Keep primary actions visible and easy to reach on mobile.

Accessibility:
- Use semantic HTML.
- Add proper labels, ARIA attributes, keyboard navigation, and visible focus rings.
- Maintain strong color contrast.
- Do not communicate meaning through color alone.
- Ensure Urdu content uses correct RTL direction and alignment.

Technical constraints:
- Preserve existing routes and functionality.
- Do not remove the current upload flow, analysis result structure, AI mentor behavior, or error handling.
- Reuse the existing component system and Tailwind styling where possible.
- Create reusable components for cards, badges, buttons, section headers, upload states, result rows, and empty states.
- Keep the code clean, typed, and maintainable.
- Do not add unnecessary dependencies.
- Verify the app builds successfully after the redesign.
- Test the homepage, upload UI, results UI, How It Works page, Mentor page, mobile navigation, and all error states.

export function Reveal({ children, className, delay = 0, as: Tag = "div" }: {...}) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    const node = ref.current;
    if (!node) return;
    if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches) { setShown(true); return; }
    const io = new IntersectionObserver(([entry]) => { if (entry.isIntersecting) { setShown(true); io.disconnect(); } }, { threshold: 0.12, rootMargin: "0px 0px -40px 0px" });

    return () => io.disconnect();
  }, []);
  return <Tag ref={ref} className={cn("transition-all duration-700 ease-out will-change-transform", shown ? "translate-y-0 opacity-100" : "translate-y-5 opacity-0", className)} style={{ transitionDelay: delay ? `${delay}ms` : undefined }}>{children}</Tag>;

The newline-method call is being misparsed — actually the error is probably because `["..."]` array literal followed by `.map(...)` on the next line is fine, but the parser may misinterpret `.map` on the following line as a property access on the previous statement boundary. In JS, a line starting with `.` is fine after an expression when not ASI-separated... but here the array ends the JSX expression? No wait, the `{...}` braces contain JSX expression. Inside, `{["..."]}.map(...)` — the `.map` refers to... hmm, the actual expression is a JSX child `{["Up to 12 MB", "Private & secure", "English + Urdu"]}` which is an element; trailing `.map` isn't valid as a separate statement. That's the bug — this parses the array as an element child and `.map` becomes a new expression statement. I need to make it a single expression. Fix: put `.map` on same line as the array.
